title: AI Data Center Debt Hits $1.3 Trillion Threatening Investors
summary:
Borrowed capital has become the primary engine for the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence facilities across the United States. Developers have raised at least $1.3T in debt to finance this growth, which a Columbia University economist warns could trigger investor wipeouts if asset values drop by 10%. This reliance on leverage creates systemic risk as the industry consumes scarce electricity and labor, potentially increasing costs for other business sectors.

Total investment in data centers and related systems will hit $10.3T through 2032, averaging 3.63% of annual GDP. This spending intensity exceeds that of the historic canal, railroad, and electric grid buildouts combined. To secure a standard 10% return on this capital, the sector requires approximately $3.7T in annual revenue by 2032, a figure that far exceeds the current combined earnings of OpenAI and Anthropic.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Data center developers have already raised at least $1.3 trillion in debt
selectedTweets.text:
🇺🇸 America is on track to pour more into AI data centers than it ever spent on railroads, electricity or the internet.

At their peak, the railroads that stitched America together ate up about 2.4% of the U.S. economy, while the dot-com boom came in at around 1.1%.

AI is headed for 2.8%, about as much as America spends on its entire military, with the bill expected to run anywhere from $2.8 trillion to over $10 trillion.

A lot of it is running on borrowed money. 

Data center developers have already raised at least $1.3 trillion in debt, and a Columbia economist warns that a 10% drop in values would be enough to start wiping people out.

The railroad boom gave America the Gilded Age, and then it gave America the Panic of 1893.

Source: Forbes / Writer: Julie

selectedTweets.text:
The AI buildout is becoming the largest infrastructure boom in US history:

AI infrastructure spending is projected to average 3.63% of US GDP annually from 2025 to 2032, far exceeding the investment intensity of previous major infrastructure booms.

By comparison, railroads averaged 2.24% of GDP from 1870-1890, highways 1.13% from 1956-1973, while telecom and fiber averaged 1.1% from 1996-2003.

This comes as total investment in data centers and related AI infrastructure is projected to reach $10.3 trillion over this period.

The spending is driven by the rapid construction of data centers and the infrastructure required to support increasingly large AI systems.

However, this expansion is consuming scarce labor and electricity, increasing costs for other businesses and crowding out other investment.

The scale of the AI investment is extraordinary, but so is the economic risk if the spending fails to generate sufficient returns.
